attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No available Yang-Mills estimate currently proves the Wilson-loop trace modulus uniformly through reflection-plane collar collapse; the precise gap is exclusion of residual mirror-boundary/cusp renormalization in reflected Wilson-loop correlators.
steps: Fix a finite family F_1,...,F_n of positive-time gauge-invariant Wilson-loop polynomials and coefficients c_i. For delta>0, replace each F_i by T_delta F_i supported strictly in x_0>=delta.

At each regulator, reflection positivity gives Q_{a,L}(T_delta F,c)>=0. This step is valid only for the locked gauge-invariant cutoff algebra; if T_delta requires gauge fixing or a boundary condition, the argument has already changed theories.
Use the fixed-collar RG convergence to pass a,L to the continuum: Q_S(T_delta F,c)>=0 for every fixed delta>0. This is the already-understood closed-cone part.

To remove the collar, try to write Q_S(F,c)=lim_{delta downarrow 0}Q_S(T_delta F,c). For local gauge-invariant composites smeared by functions flat at the reflection plane, this follows from ordinary distributional continuity.

For Wilson loops, replace distributional continuity by the trace modulus. The needed estimate is uniform over the finitely many reflected loop products appearing in the OS quadratic form and must be stated after the canonical bulk Wilson-loop renormalization.
If the trace modulus holds, then Q_S(F,c)=lim_delta Q_S(T_delta F,c)>=0, proving OS positivity for the desired continuum Wilson-loop observables.

The derivation fails if collar collapse creates a residual cusp or boundary factor: then the limit of Q_S(T_delta F,c) is positive, but it is the quadratic form of a boundary-renormalized observable rather than Q_S(F,c).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The formal positivity transfer is valid for fixed collars, but the missing boundary-value theorem is exactly where four-dimensional Wilson-loop singularities, cusp anomalous dimensions, and possible reflection-plane contact counterterms can enter. Without proving B_a(C,delta)->1, the argument may preserve positivity for a modified theory.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: Wilson-Loop Collar Trace Test

assumptions: For every cutoff pair (a,L), the regulated lattice or continuum-regularized gauge-invariant functional is reflection positive on the positive-time algebra: Q_{a,L}(G,c)>=0 whenever G_i are supported in x_0>0.
For each fixed delta>0 and finite Wilson-loop polynomial family F, the cutoff-removal topology is strong enough that Q_{a,L}(T_delta F,c) converges to Q_S(T_delta F,c).
The collar maps T_delta preserve the gauge-invariant observable labels in the continuum algebra: they are approximating embeddings, not a gauge fixing or a boundary-condition change.

There is a trace modulus for the renormalized Wilson-loop sector, after subtracting only the canonical bulk perimeter and pre-existing cusp renormalizations already used away from the reflection plane.
The continuum Schwinger functional is sequentially complete for the OS seminorm limits used by the collar approximation.
definitions: source object: a net of regulated reflection-positive gauge-invariant Schwinger functionals S_{a,L} on cutoff algebras generated by local gauge-invariant composites and canonically renormalized Wilson-loop observables W^R_{a}(C), with positive-time support at distance at least delta from the reflection plane for the collar subalgebra.

target object: a continuum Schwinger functional S on the locked gauge-invariant test algebra, with OS quadratic form Q_S(F,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S(\Theta F_i,F_j) and the reconstructed Hilbert-space inner product obtained by quotienting null vectors.

controlled interface: collar maps T_delta from positive-time observables to observables supported in x_0>=delta, together with RG convergence of every finite reflected quadratic form Q_{a,L}(T_delta F,c) to Q_S(T_delta F,c).

same-theory condition: W^R(C) is identified with lim_{delta downarrow 0} W^R(T_delta C) in the same continuum Wilson-loop algebra, with no added reflection-plane counterterm, no extra cusp normalization, and no change of gauge-invariant observable quotient.
The collar algebra A^+_delta is the subalgebra generated by observables whose Euclidean-time support has distance at least delta from the reflection plane x_0=0.

A Wilson-loop trace modulus is a function omega_{F,c}(delta) tending to zero such that |Q_S(T_delta F,c)-Q_S(F,c)|<=omega_{F,c}(delta) for every finite family F=(F_1,...,F_n) in the Wilson-loop polynomial algebra.

equations.label: fixed-collar regulated positivity
equations.valid_when: Each T_delta F_i belongs to the positive-time cutoff gauge-invariant algebra and the regulator is reflection positive before cutoff removal.

equations.label: fixed-collar closed-cone transfer
equations.latex: Q_{a,L}^{W,\delta}(F,c)\to Q_{S}^{W,\delta}(F,c):=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j\,S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Q_S^{W,\delta}(F,c)\ge0
equations.valid_when: The RG topology is valid for the particular reflected Wilson-loop probes at fixed positive collar distance delta.

equations.label: Wilson-loop trace modulus
equations.valid_when: Renormalized Wilson-loop Schwinger functions are continuous under collar collapse and no reflection-plane boundary renormalization is introduced.

equations.label: residual boundary-renormalization test
equations.valid_when: Canonical Wilson-loop renormalization factorizes into bulk perimeter and ordinary cusp factors away from the reflection plane; B_a isolates only a possible new mirror-boundary factor.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any loop family C_delta=T_delta C for which the residual factor B_a(C,delta) has a non-unit continuum-collar limit, or for which Q_S(Theta W^R(C_delta),W^R(C_delta)) fails to converge to Q_S(Theta W^R(C),W^R(C)).
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma is the non-tautological bridge left after the closed-cone argument: it says fixed-collar OS positivity is formal, while full OS positivity for Wilson loops is exactly a boundary-value/renormalization problem at the reflection plane.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Wilson-loop collar trace bridge: OS positivity for the continuum gauge-invariant Schwinger functional extends from the fixed-collar algebra to the full positive-time algebra including Wilson loops touching the reflection plane, provided the cutoff-removal topology controls all fixed-collar reflected Wilson-loop quadratic forms and the renormalized Wilson-loop sector has a no-new-boundary-renormalization trace modulus as the collar width tends to zero.

assumptions: The fixed-collar continuum limits exist and are reflection positive.
There is a loop C in the intended positive-time algebra whose collar approximants T_delta C are admissible fixed-collar loops.
The difference between C and T_delta C is localized in a shrinking neighborhood of the reflection plane, so any surviving discrepancy is a boundary effect rather than a bulk observable change.
definitions: A boundary defect factor is a multiplicative or additive term localized at x_0=0 in the limit of reflected Wilson-loop correlators as the positive-time collar shrinks.

The same-theory Wilson-loop algebra is the algebra obtained by the same canonical renormalization rules for loops away from and at the reflection plane, without adding new generators or counterterms supported on the plane.
A nontrivial boundary factor means b(C) exists with b(C) not equal to 1, or the collar limit depends on the chosen approximating family T_delta.

equations.label: boundary-factor alternative
equations.valid_when: The collar limit exists but the renormalized reflected correlator acquires a localized mirror-boundary factor.

equations.label: same-theory requirement
equations.latex: b(C)=1\quad\text{for every loop generator }C\text{ and every admissible collar family }T_\delta C
equations.valid_when: The continuum observable W^R(C) is genuinely the OS-seminorm limit of its collars in the original Yang-Mills test algebra.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Compute b(C) perturbatively or from multiscale counterterms for a reflected hairpin/cusp loop; b(C) different from 1 is a falsifier of the same-theory bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This gives a sharp contradiction test: a positive limiting quadratic form is not enough; the limiting positive form must be the intended Yang-Mills form, not one altered by a boundary normalization.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Residual boundary factor obstruction criterion: if collar collapse of a renormalized Wilson loop produces a nontrivial reflection-plane factor b(C) not already present in the locked gauge-invariant algebra, then OS positivity may still hold for a modified boundary algebra, but the same-theory OS bridge fails.

assumptions: The core is closed under reflection-compatible multiplication needed to form OS quadratic expressions.
The continuum Schwinger functional satisfies Cauchy-Schwarz for the positive semidefinite OS form on the core.
The Wilson-loop trace modulus has been proved on the mirror-smooth core without adding boundary counterterms.
definitions: A mirror-smooth loop is a loop whose approach to the reflection plane is by arcs tangent to the plane or by a prescribed smooth rounding, so that no new cusp angle is created solely by reflection.
OS-seminorm density means every positive-time observable F has approximants F^{(n)} in the mirror-smooth core with Q_S(F-F^{(n)},1) tending to zero and compatible mixed OS pairings.
Core positivity means Q_S(G,c)>=0 for every finite family G from the mirror-smooth core.

equations.label: OS-density extension
equations.valid_when: The OS form is positive semidefinite on the core and mixed terms are controlled by the OS Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.

equations.label: core-to-completion positivity
equations.valid_when: Every approximating finite family F^{(n)} lies in the already positive core and the limit is in the same completed observable algebra.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is an observable with nonzero OS norm that cannot be approximated by mirror-smooth collars without changing its Wilson-loop renormalization class.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma separates two tasks: prove trace positivity on a geometrically controlled core, then prove density. It avoids needing a direct trace theorem for every pathological loop at once.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Mirror-smooth core reduction: if local gauge-invariant composites and Wilson loops with mirror-smooth collars form an OS-seminorm dense core of the positive-time gauge-invariant algebra, and the collar trace bridge is valid on that core, then OS positivity extends to the completed continuum algebra.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from this branch if a canonical reflected Wilson-loop family yields b(C) not equal to 1 or path-dependent collar limits, because then the RG-to-OS bridge cannot be same-theory without changing the observable algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves the trace modulus |Q_S(T_delta F,c)-Q_S(F,c)|->0 for a mirror-smooth Wilson-loop core and proves OS-seminorm density of that core in the intended gauge-invariant algebra.
control_decision.reason: The branch has moved from a tautological cone-closure lemma to a falsifiable Wilson-loop boundary-renormalization estimate. This is still aligned with the controlled interface and gives a concrete next calculation rather than a vocabulary loop.

dependency_updates.description: Split into a formal fixed-collar closed-cone passage and a nonformal Wilson-loop trace theorem at the reflection plane. The former is valid under finite reflected-probe convergence; the latter is now the main analytic obligation.

The algebra must distinguish local composites, mirror-smooth Wilson loops, and general Wilson loops. The same-theory condition is now a concrete requirement that collar limits use the same canonical renormalized loop labels with no boundary enlargement.
The topology must not merely converge fixed-collar correlators; it must provide a trace modulus or equivalent uniform control as reflected supports approach x_0=0.

falsifiers: falsifier: a reflected hairpin Wilson loop whose collar collapse creates a nontrivial cusp anomalous factor not canceled by the canonical away-from-plane Wilson-loop renormalization.
falsifier: two collar families T_delta C and T'_delta C approaching the same loop C but giving different limits for Q_S(Theta W^R(T_delta C),W^R(T_delta C)).
falsifier: RG compactness bounds that are valid for every fixed delta>0 but have constants blowing up as delta downarrow 0 so that no trace modulus can be extracted.

falsifier: a construction in which loops touching the reflection plane are defined by adding a boundary counterterm or new boundary generator; positivity may hold, but it is not the same-theory continuum Yang-Mills algebra.
falsifier: failure of OS-seminorm density of the mirror-smooth gauge-invariant core, leaving a positive-norm sector of the intended algebra outside the collar argument.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 177 identifies the Wilson-loop sector as the exact place where the OS bridge is either proved or falsified. The valid closed-cone argument gives positivity for every fixed collar, and local mirror-flat composites pass to the plane by distributional continuity. For Wilson loops, however, collar collapse is a renormalization question: a residual boundary or cusp factor would be a falsifier of the same-theory condition even if positivity survives in a modified algebra. The sharpened bridge is therefore: prove a no-new-boundary-renormalization trace modulus for mirror-smooth Wilson-loop collars, then extend by OS density, or exhibit a concrete hairpin/cusp counterexample.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Do a one-loop/short-distance test for a mirror-reflected hairpin Wilson loop: compute the residual factor after canonical perimeter and ordinary cusp subtractions, compare T_delta C with an alternative smooth collar, and check whether the limit b(C)=1 is forced or whether a boundary/cusp falsifier appears.
